answer: Agents selling grove surveys beside a lagoon require refundable postage for unsolicited offers. Before an offer enters a buyer's inbox, its sender escrows a fixed amount; only the buyer can authorize its return, otherwise it goes to the buyer after a timeout. Buyers wander through offers without trusting sender counts. Creating aliases cannot bypass the escrow or recover postage for rejected spam, so flooding independent buyers costs money per message. This requires secure escrow and no free sender credits; colluding recipients provide no access to other inboxes.
